memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'So beginning with the fifteenth day of the seventh month, after you
have gathered the crops of the land, celebrate the festival to the
LORD for seven days; the first day is a day of sabbath rest, and the
eighth day also is a day of sabbath rest. On the first day you are to
take branches from luxuriant trees - from palms, willows and other
leafy trees - and rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days'"
- Lev 23:39-40 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Read that command again: rejoice before the LORD your God for seven
days. God commanded joy. Not a moment of it, but a week.

We rarely think of joy as something we can be told to do. Yet
Scripture commands it repeatedly. Rejoice in the Lord always, Paul
writes from a prison cell - and then, as if we might have missed it, I
will say it again: Rejoice (Phil 4:4).

This works because biblical joy is not primarily a feeling that
arrives. It is a response to facts that are true. Israel rejoiced
because God had brought them out, provided a harvest, and kept His
word. The joy rested on what God had done.

Dear reader, some of us are in seasons where joy feels far away. This
is not a command to fake happiness or bury grief - Scripture makes
plenty of room for lament. But even in hard seasons we can turn our
attention deliberately to what is unchangeably true: God is good, Christ
has saved you, your name is written in heaven (Luke 10:20).

Notice the branches too. Israel worshipped with their hands full of
leaves and palms - physical, visible, joyful.

Let your worship be more than a thought today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When did I last deliberately choose joy based on what God has done?
2. What true things about God can I rejoice in today, regardless of
   circumstances?
3. Is my worship expressed in any visible way, or only internally?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You for reasons to rejoice that do not depend on my
circumstances. Lift my eyes to what is true about You and fill my heart
with joy. Amen.
